answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity through staked, decaying reputation rather than free accounts. Think of each agent's history as a garden: trust grows only through verified work over time, and a new clone starts barren. An onyx-grade bond, collateral locked and slashed on proven fraud, makes spinning up thousands of fake identities expensive, since each copy must post real value. An atlas of attestations ties that history together, so an attacker cannot abandon a burned reputation and reappear at full standing; the cost compounds with every fake.
